a10_note: Still applies (nothing refuses a terminal state followed by an open one for the same id); store-discipline family, E14. EVIDENCE: MEASURED 2026-09-24: grep weaker|revert in scripts/ops/pipeline.py -> none.

due_when.clears_when: scripts/ops/pipeline.py --check (or a new check beside it) FAILS when a record's resolved state is weaker than a state that same id already reached earlier in the file -- i.e. a terminal state (done/killed) followed by an open one (queued/due/routed) for the same id is refused or at minimum reported as an error rather than validating clean. A merge-procedure doc note alone does NOT clear this: the failure mode is that nobody looks, so the fix has to be the guard, not the instruction. Additionally: the one-off audit in origin.rerun has been run over the whole store and its result recorded here, so we know whether any EXISTING row was already reverted this way.

origin.rerun:
REPRODUCE THE SILENT REVERT (no VM, no network):
  1. From a branch that has appended a STATE UPDATE to an id whose ORIGINAL record also reached main by
     another PR, run: git merge origin/main --no-commit --no-ff
  2. Resolve docs/claude/work/PIPELINE.jsonl by the documented rule -- common prefix once, then OURS'
     tail, then THEIRS' tail, deduplicating nothing.
  3. python3 -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'scripts/ops');import pipeline;"
     "print(pipeline.read_log().items['<the id>']['state'])"
     -> prints the OLD state, because theirs' copy is now last and the store resolves last-wins.
  4. python3 scripts/ops/pipeline.py --check -> exit 0. The guard does not see it.
MEASURED 2026-09-24 on PI-20260924-JN54P2HH-0003: appended `done` on the branch at merged line 1328, main's original `queued` copy landed at line 1400, and read_log() reported `queued`.
AUDIT THE STORE FOR EXISTING INSTANCES:
  python3 -c "import json,collections;recs=[json.loads(l) for l in open('docs/claude/work/PIPELINE.jsonl') if l.strip() and not l.startswith('//')];"
  "seen=collections.defaultdict(list);\nfor i,r in enumerate(recs): seen[r['id']].append((i,r.get('state')));"
  "\nfor k,v in seen.items():\n  st=[s for _,s in v]\n  if 'done' in st[:-1] or 'killed' in st[:-1]:\n    print(k,st)"
  -- any id whose LAST state is weaker than an earlier one is a candidate revert.

what:
THE PIPELINE'S OWN MERGE RULE CAN SILENTLY REVERT A RECORD'S STATE, AND NEITHER --check NOR ANY GUARD SEES IT. The store is the repo's follow-through mechanism; a row that quietly goes from `done` back to `queued` is survivable, but the same mechanism can take a row from `killed` or `routed` back to open, or -- the direction that actually costs -- leave a row LOOKING open when it was closed, or looking closed when a later session reopened it.
THE MECHANISM, and both halves are individually correct:
  (a) The documented conflict resolution for docs/claude/work/PIPELINE.jsonl is LINE UNION -- common prefix once, then BOTH tails, deduplicate NOTHING. That rule exists because a repeated id is a later STATE UPDATE, not a duplicate, and dropping one loses history. It is right.
  (b) read_log() resolves an id's CURRENT state by LAST WINS -- the last record for an id in file order. Also right, given (a).
Together they are not. The union appends OURS' tail then THEIRS' tail, so file order after a merge encodes which SIDE a record came from, not WHEN it was written. If both sides' tails contain the same id -- which happens whenever a record reaches main by one PR while a branch also carries it, i.e. routinely -- the OLDER copy can end up last and win.
MEASURED 2026-09-24, not hypothesised: merging origin/main into claude/e41-strip-inert-trail-decay-arms, this branch's PI-20260924-JN54P2HH-0003 state=`done` landed at line 1328 and main's original state=`queued` copy at line 1400. read_log() then reported `queued`. Lines 1323-1329 and 1396-1401 hold the same four ids on both sides. Nothing was LOST -- every record survives, as the rule intends -- but the resolved state was wrong.
WHY IT IS INVISIBLE: pipeline.py --check validates each record and reports id collisions against _identity_mismatches, but it never asserts that an id's resolved state is at least as advanced as any state that id previously reached. Exit 0 on the reverted file. This was caught only because an unrelated assertion about the record's text happened to fail -- i.e. by luck, which is the part that makes it worth filing rather than fixing in place.
FIXED HERE FOR THIS ONE ROW, ADDITIVELY: the `done` state was re-appended at the end of the merged file. Nothing was rewritten and no record was deleted.
[!] WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any EXISTING row in the store is already sitting in a reverted state from an earlier merge. The store is 1402 lines over 1259 ids and I did not audit it -- the one-off audit command is in origin.rerun and running it is part of what clears this row. Until then, treat a `queued` row that looks like it should have been closed as possibly reverted rather than possibly forgotten.

── [SHARPENED 2026-09-24, same merge] THE RULE AS WRITTEN ALSO FAILS THE GUARD, so it is not merely imprecise -- it is unfollowable, and a session that follows it literally lands a store that CI rejects.
MEASURED: `pipeline.py --check` exits 0 on BOTH sides in isolation (cbebacca8 -> exit 0, 0 NEW collisions; origin/main -> exit 0, 0 NEW collisions) and exits 1 with 4 NEW collisions on their literal line union. The collisions read 'what changed (not an append-only extension of the prior text)' -- produced when a byte-identical re-delivery of a record lands AFTER a later update of that same id, so the append-only check sees a long `what` followed by the short original.
ROOT CAUSE, and it is the same one: OURS and THEIRS both carried the same records, because a long-lived branch merges main repeatedly and each merge re-appends main's tail. MEASURED on this file: main carries 14 duplicate-line groups / 15 extra lines, while the literal union carried 56 groups / 87 extra lines, some ids appearing FOUR and SIX times verbatim. Of THEIRS' 72 tail lines, **71 were byte-identical to lines already present** and exactly ONE was new.
RESOLUTION APPLIED HERE, narrow and provable: drop a line from THEIRS' tail only when a byte-identical line already exists in the merged result. This cannot lose a record -- the line survives verbatim, which is asserted in code before writing (every distinct line of head, theirs and the local appends must be present in the output). Result: 1403 -> 1332 lines, --check exit 0, 0 NEW collisions, 1261 items, zero ids from either side missing, and PI-20260924-JN54P2HH-0003 correctly resolving to `done`.
⚠️ THIS DOES NOT DEDUPE THE STORE, deliberately. The 15 pre-existing duplicate groups on main are untouched; only re-deliveries introduced BY THIS MERGE were dropped. A general dedupe of the shared register is a separate change and does not belong in a Tier-3 strategy PR.
WHAT THIS ROW NOW ASKS FOR is therefore two things, not one: (1) the state-regression check in `clears_when` above, and (2) the merge rule in the docs amended from 'deduplicate NOTHING' to 'deduplicate nothing but an exact byte-identical line already present', with the lossless assertion written into the resolver rather than left to each session to re-derive.
